source.title: The Effect of Mini-Batch Noise on the Implicit Bias of Adam

record.tranche_reason: The experiments vary Adam’s momentum hyperparameters and batch size, then report validation performance and sharpness measures. They test batch-dependent generalization outcomes using a different setup from the claim’s large-batch comparisons.
record.gate_note: Theoretical derivations and cited prior studies are not rows. Experiment values are plotted in figures; the text describes the qualitative trends but gives no exact plotted validation values.
record.test_reason: The Llama3 experiments compare held-out loss at batch sizes 64 and 1024 after the same single pass over about 25 billion tokens. Figure 3 shows worse loss for the larger batch across the displayed beta sweep, bearing on V5. The WikiText-2 minimum-over-training comparisons do not hold epochs fixed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors derive a directional reversal in Adam's implicit sharpness bias as mini-batch noise changes, and report qualitatively consistent language-model experiments. The theory uses explicit approximations. Downstream fine-tuning and quantization benefits are suggested, not measured.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments sweep Adam or AdamW beta settings across batch sizes and examine validation performance and sharpness; they do not reproduce the fixed-epoch large-batch comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation-performance trend changes with batch size and the swept beta setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing beta2 generally improves minimum validation perplexity at small batches, with the direction reversing as batch size increases; the appendix reports an analogous beta1 reversal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam's preferred momentum settings for language-model validation performance depend on batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-adaptive sharpness and gradient norms accompany validation-loss changes in the Transformer experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-adaptive sharpness can track validation loss across Adam momentum settings in these language-model experiments.

record.problems: The reported experiment outcomes are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The small-Transformer validation perplexity is averaged over three iterations, and no error bars are stated. The Llama3 section says a train/validation performance gap is not applicable.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated experiment results were left out. Figure-only sharpness and gradient-norm measurements are not extracted because they do not measure the validation-performance outcome in V5.

untested.parts: Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Image classifiers, fixed multi-epoch comparisons, the workload-dependent threshold, and whether longer training or recipe adaptation closes the batch penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings within a convolutional family, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's combined limits_scope verdict: beta-dependent performance alone does not establish a limitation of V5. Equal single-pass token budgets do provide the fixed-data-exposure comparison that the record incorrectly lists as entirely untested. The study does not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness named by V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Image classifiers; comparisons at a fixed epoch budget; large-batch penalties independent of changes to Adam’s beta settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based generalization measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining.

reader_labels.condition: WikiText-2 small Transformer and Llama3 DCLM pretraining across tested batch sizes
reader_labels.reason: The text reports that larger β2 mostly helps at small batch sizes and that this behavior transitions to the opposite as batch size increases; this indicates batch-dependent optimizer settings matter (R1–R8), without establishing a fixed-epoch large-batch penalty.
